chapter: Queens Terrace, Decca records and Amen
title: Sunnyside Horseshoe and the first recordings in 1940
summary: After the fire he moves to the Horseshoe and begins recording in 1940.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And you got burned out in the World's Fair.
That's right, the latter part of '39, and we went across the street, where we got burned out, and that's when we went into Sunnyside Horseshoe and that's where I had Don Stovall.
That's about the time that you started recording.
That's right, that was my first recording.
It had to be because the World's Fair was '39 and '40.
You would have been in the Horseshoe Bar in Sunnyside?
In the Horseshoe Bar; that's right.
Didn't you play some place in Brooklyn around that time too, or did Brooklyn come later?
That's where I saw-- well, no, that's way later that I saw you there. Some ugly broad say she was Louie Prima's wife.
Yeah. She did. I remember that.
